newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Germany says agreed lira level matches economy.
newsitem.headline: Germany says agreed lira level matches economy.

text.p: Top German monetary officials said on Sunday the agreed lira entry level for the Exchange Rate Mechanism, at 990 per mark, was a better match to the Italian economy than a weaker rate earlier sought by Rome.
Bundesbank head Hans Tietmeyer told reporters that the lira's return to the ERM was not prejudging Italy' ability to join the first wave of a future joint currency in Europe.

Juergen Stark, state secretary at the German finance ministry, made clear in his remarks that Italy had made the negotiations more difficult for itself by making many public comments in advance of the talks and coming to Brussels with a rigid position.

But he added that Italy's decision to enter the ERM, which follows soon after a similar move by Finland, showed that both countries took seriously the criterion on currency rates laid down for entry to monetary union.
The German delegation nonetheless made clear that Italy had not gained an open ticket to join monetary union in 1999.
"This is not a prejudicial decision. It is certainly not a comment on Italy's qualification for monetary union," Tietmeyer told reporters after the talks.
The two German officials added that Italy's European partners had made clear to Italy that it must do more to cut back on its budget deficits.

Tietmeyer commented particularly on a comment in the official communique released after the meeting, which noted that the "Italian authorities are committed to intensify their efforts to complete the adjustment of their economy."
"They committed to INTENSIFY their efforts," Tietmeyer said, stressing that this meant that increased effort must be made.
